newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi index and turnover fall in calm trading.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi index and turnover fall in calm trading.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index and turnover fell on Tuesday in a calm market.
The the index fell 11.78 points to 3078.05 while turnover was posted at 11.477 million shillings on 375,517 compared to 24.121 million shillings on 566,184 shares on Monday.

Nairobi Stock Exchange chairman Jimnah Mbaru said national carrier Kenya Airways, first traded on the bourse on June 3, had been included in the 20-share index list. Kenya Airways replaces Cooper Motor Corporation Holdings.
"The Airline shares have become the most active traded with an average daily turnover of 2.2 million shillings, constituting 25 percent of the average daily turnover," Mbaru said.

"At the current prices, the airline has a market capitalisation of 4.7 billion shillings, thus making it one of the top 20 highly capitalised companies on the Nairobi Stock Exchange," Mbaru said in a statement.

"In many ways the index mirrors the performance of the economy as a whole while also reflecting the mood of investors. The inclusion of Kenya Airways in the index will make the index more up to date," added Mbaru, also chairman of leading brokerage concern, Dyer & Blair Ltd.

Meantime, the International Finance Company has begun to calculate the index for Kenya in line with its policy of encouraging international investors to look at and invest in emerging markets. The IFC index will contitute 17 companies.
Kenya Airways fell 10 cents to 10 on 43,166 shares while CMC Holdings held steady at 63.
Uchumi Supermarket fell a shilling to 39.
There was good trading of shares on Firestone East Africa from foreign investor interest and alot of demand for its shares due to its high dividend yields, brokers said.
"Firestone East Africa has a strong growth prospect. It has got a monopoly in the region (East Africa), a broker said, explaining while the tyre firm motivated investors.

Firestone traded 204,995 shares unchanged at 28, Total Kenya eased to 70 from 71.50. Kenya Power was unchanged at 120 and brokers said despite rationing of power, the power firm was bound to remain stable because it was a monopoly.
Among the plantations, George Williamson rose a shilling to 67, Kakuzi fell to 95 from 95.50 while Rea Vipingo was unchanged at 10.80 on 14,200 shares.
Barclays Bank fell 3.0 shillings to 101, Kenya Commercial Bank rose to 52.50 from 52 and Housing Finance eased to 23 from 23.50.
